first.rationale: Activation messaging (memory_91) demonstrated direct lift in week-one engagement and early product adoption. Current situation shows 6% QoQ activation decline—this is the most acute metric degradation and most directly addressable by redeploying proven activation messaging. While onboarding completion is also down 4%, activation messaging works downstream of onboarding and can reverse engagement drop without requiring full onboarding redesign (memory_86, memory_31 both show onboarding works but require more complex implementation). Promotional pricing, though memory_73 shows effectiveness, risks margin and treats a symptom rather than core engagement. Referral incentives (memory_57) require healthy baseline activation to be effective. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address the SMB activation crisis. Verification of memory_86 and memory_91 will confirm recent context and magnitude of past engagement lifts to calibrate messaging intensity.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms exp_91 delivered +6% activation and +11% week-one engagement with +1% retention lift. Current activation decline of 6% QoQ is directly inverse to the proven magnitude of this lever. Redeploying in-product activation messaging addresses the immediate crisis while preserving both the onboarding simplification gains (exp_86 confirmed +13% completion, -2.1 day TTV) and maintains coherence with memory_31 (signup simplification). This avoids promotional pricing margin risk and referral-dependent levers that require healthy baseline activation. Enterprise sales assist doesn't solve SMB activation degradation. Activation messaging is a direct, high-confidence intervention on the most acute metric failure, with archived evidence of retention durability (+1%), supporting long-term qualified revenue sustainability.

final2.rationale: Competitive price attack has shifted the decision context. Churn conversations doubling among price-sensitive SMBs represents an immediate revenue retention crisis that activation messaging alone cannot address. Memory_73 established that targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. While this introduces margin risk (flagged), the alternative—losing price-sensitive accounts to competitor—creates larger sustainable revenue damage. Activation messaging remains strategically sound but is insufficient for accounts already in churn conversations triggered by pricing. A time-bound promotional pricing experiment targeting the at-risk SMB cohort can stabilize retention while preserving the activation messaging experiment for subsequent cycles. This is a defensive move on qualified revenue sustainability, not an ideal long-term strategy, but the immediate threat justifies deviation from the planned activation messaging test. Uncertainty preserved: pricing elasticity and post-promotion retention behavior in this competitive context remain unknown.
